decisions.quote:
Unexpectedly and partially in contrast with Bruneau et al.’s work, affective prejudice 

was found to be related to discrimination such that pre-service teachers who had colder 

feelings towards Roma were more likely to discriminate against them in educational-track 

recommendations. One explanation for this discrepancy concerns the role of the context in 

which these associations were studied. Despite negative perceptions toward Romani people

 DRIVERS OF TEACHER DISCRIMINATION 

are widespread across Europe, arguably, Germany is a less openly Romani-hostile context 

than Hungary and thus dehumanization insights may be less accurate in describing underlying 

discriminatory behaviors (Enock et al., 2021). It is important to note that in Bruneau et al.’s 

work blatant dehumanization (but not infrahumanization) predicted teacher biased educational 

recommendations. In our conceptual replication we could not directly test this finding because 

the measure of blatant dehumanization raised ethical concerns.
decisions.location: Primary Discussion, affective-prejudice comparison and omitted blatant-dehumanization measure
decisions.reason: The primary study confirms the original Romani educational-track discrimination and expressly contrasts the positive affective-prejudice association here with the original null. Those original-specific comparisons support mixed. The original also found no infrahumanization association, so the current null agrees; failure of the new contextual H2 is not an original-specific replication failure. The original blatant-dehumanization measure was ethically omitted here and could not be directly retested. Preserve these limits; do not treat absent testing as a failed effect. This independent parent rationale replaces the expert rationale while preserving its raw opinion and retaining the same mixed label.
